Respiratory Disorders

Respiratory disorders — COPD, asthma, pneumonia, tuberculosis — assessment and nursing care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe COPD, asthma, pneumonia and tuberculosis
  • State nursing care for respiratory patients
  • Explain oxygen therapy and breathing exercises

In simple words

Respiratory disorders affect the airways and lungs — making breathing difficult. Nurses assess breathing, give oxygen, teach breathing exercises and monitor for deterioration.

Common disorders: COPD, asthma, pneumonia, tuberculosis.

Common respiratory disorders

Disorder Cause/Features Key signs
COPD Chronic bronchitis + emphysema; smoking Breathlessness, chronic cough, wheeze
Asthma Airway inflammation, reversible narrowing Wheeze, cough, chest tightness, triggered by allergens
Pneumonia Lung infection (bacterial/viral) Fever, cough, breathlessness, chest pain, consolidation
Tuberculosis (TB) Mycobacterium tuberculosis Chronic cough >2 weeks, weight loss, night sweats, haemoptysis

Nursing care

  • Position upright — improves lung expansion.
  • Oxygen therapy — as prescribed; monitor SpO2 (target 88–92% in COPD, 94–98% otherwise).
  • Breathing exercises — deep breathing, pursed-lip breathing, incentive spirometer.
  • Coughing and clearance — encourage effective coughing; suction if needed.
  • Hydration — encourages thin secretions (unless fluid-restricted).

Tuberculosis care

  • Airborne precautions — mask, isolation.
  • Sputum collection — early morning, before antibiotics.
  • DOTS — observe treatment; 6–9 months; adherence critical.
  • Patient teaching — cover mouth when coughing, dispose of sputum safely, complete treatment.

🔴 Oxygen in COPD

In COPD, give controlled oxygen — target SpO2 88–92% (not 100%). High-flow oxygen can remove the hypoxic drive to breathe in some COPD patients.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Assess breathing — rate, depth, pattern, use of accessory muscles, colour, SpO2.
  • Position upright — Fowler’s position improves breathing.
  • Oxygen — as prescribed; never adjust flow without orders; humidify.
  • Breathing exercises — teach deep breathing, pursed-lip breathing, incentive spirometer use.
  • TB infection control — airborne precautions, mask, sputum precautions, DOTS adherence.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. COPD = chronic bronchitis + emphysema; smoking is the main cause.
  2. Asthma = reversible airway narrowing, triggered by allergens.
  3. Pneumonia = lung infection with consolidation; fever, cough, breathlessness.
  4. TB = chronic cough >2 weeks, weight loss, night sweats, haemoptysis.
  5. Position upright; oxygen as prescribed; monitor SpO2.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. In COPD, target SpO2 88–92% (controlled oxygen).
  2. Pursed-lip breathing helps control breathlessness.
  3. Incentive spirometer prevents atelectasis after surgery.
  4. TB: airborne precautions, sputum precautions, DOTS adherence (6–9 months).
  5. Encourage fluids to thin secretions (unless fluid-restricted).

📌 Memory trick

TB symptoms: “C-W-N-H” — Chronic cough, Weight loss, Night sweats, Haemoptysis.

60-second revision

  • Respiratory disorders: COPD, asthma, pneumonia, TB.
  • Position upright; oxygen as prescribed; monitor SpO2.
  • COPD: controlled oxygen 88–92%.
  • Breathing exercises: deep breathing, pursed-lip, incentive spirometer.
  • TB: airborne precautions, DOTS (6–9 months).

Test yourself

COPD is caused mainly by:

Answer: B. Smoking is the main cause of COPD (chronic bronchitis + emphysema).

In COPD, oxygen target SpO2 is:

Answer: B. In COPD, controlled oxygen targets 88–92% to avoid removing the hypoxic drive.

TB is spread by:

Answer: B. TB spreads by airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.

Pursed-lip breathing helps:

Answer: B. Pursed-lip breathing helps control breathlessness in COPD and asthma.

DOTS in TB means:

Answer: B. DOTS = Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course — watch the patient swallow every dose.
